messages:
Marta (Design): Pushed a small update to the trace viewer Figma — added inline "hypothesis" annotations next to stack frames and a tiny 'note' pill on frames. Link: https://www.figma.com/file/xxx/inline-annotations

Marta (Design): Goals: let SREs jot quick hypotheses (e.g. 'likely null from parsing'), make them discoverable in drilldowns, and include them in downloads. Need feedback on placement, affordance, export UX, and A11y.

Ryan (Design): Saw it — love the minimal pill. Only concern: it shifts layout for densely populated stack traces. Could we float the pill over the right gutter so it doesn't push text? :thinking_face:

Sam (Eng): Floating is fine technically. We should ensure the pill doesn't overlap the copy when line-wrap happens. Also need a deterministic DOM order for keyboard focus and screen readers.

Nina (A11y): Agreed — DOM order matters. If the annotation is purely decorative we can move it visually, but for a11y we want it reachable. Proposal: keep frame text first in DOM, then the annotation button. Add aria-label like "Edit hypothesis for frame: <function name>".

Alex (Product): For export: customers want snapshot parity. Two options: (1) include annotations inline in exported JSON/markdown, (2) export them as a separate CSV/notes file. I lean toward inline embedding with an opt-out toggle in the export modal.

Marta (Design): Thinking inline embedding with a small header for annotations makes it easier to share. Export modal copy: "Include developer annotations" vs "Include private notes" — which is clearer?

Nina (A11y): Avoid ambiguous words. "Include annotations (visible in trace)" is clear. Also call out sensing: "Annotations may contain PII — review before sharing."

Sam (Eng): Quick technical note: exported JSON shape suggestion (very small example):
```
{
  "trace_id": "abc",
  "frames": [
    { "id": "f1", "line": 42, "function": "parseHeader", "annotation": "possible null header" }
  ]
}
```
This keeps annotations tightly coupled to frames. We'll implement optional flag export_annotations=true.

Ryan (Design): Back to UI — keyboard nav: Tab into trace, down/up arrow to move between frames, Enter to open frame details, then focus should land on annotation button. Need a visible focus ring. Also add a shortcut 'A' when a frame is selected to quick-add annotation.

Marta (Design): Good. For visual affordance I'd prefer a subtle pencil icon inside the pill; full text shows on hover/focus. For mobile/compact view, show an icon only and open the note inline.

Nina (A11y): Screen reader behavior: when an annotation exists, announce on frame focus: "Annotation: 'possible null header' — Edit annotation (press Enter)". Implementation hint: role="region" aria-live="polite" could be used for newly added annotations. Also example aria string:
```
<button aria-label="Edit hypothesis for frame parseHeader">Edit annotation</button>
```

Alex (Product): One more product constraint — some customers will want annotations to be private to their org or only to specific members. We need to add metadata: author, created_at, visibility (team/org). For exports, default to include only team-visible annotations.

Sam (Eng): Adding meta is straightforward. We'll version the export shape: export_v2 will include annotations.meta = {author, ts, visibility}. Keep export_v1 backward compatible.

Marta (Design): Copy choices for the pill tooltip: "Hypothesis", "Note", "Annotation". Which do we land on?

Alex (Product): "Hypothesis" might sound too research-y for some customers. "Annotation" is neutral. "Note" is very casual. I'd pick "Annotation" unless design thinks otherwise.

Ryan (Design): I prefer "Hypothesis" for a11y of engineering teams — it signals intent, not just arbitrary notes. However "Annotation (Hypothesis)" as label could cover both. Eg: pill text shows icon + "Hypothesis" but tooltip says "Annotation — hypothesis".

Nina (A11y): Whatever choice, ensure the aria-label exposes both short label and purpose: e.g., aria-label="Annotation (hypothesis) — Edit".

Marta (Design): Action items: 1) Ryan to update Figma to float pill in gutter & add keyboard flow 2) Sam to prototype DOM order and export_v2 shape 3) Nina to draft SR strings and guidance for aria-live usage 4) Alex to add privacy metadata options to export modal copy.

Ryan (Design): On it — will push an updated frame comp by EOD. :white_check_mark:

Sam (Eng): I'll start a small PR for export flag and JSON shape, link soon.

Nina (A11y): I'll add sample SR announcement copy and a short checklist for devs.

Marta (Design): Thanks all — if anyone has pushback on "Annotation" vs "Hypothesis" post the reason here. Otherwise I'll prefer "Annotation (hypothesis)" for labels to keep things discoverable. :heart:

Aria-bot: deploy scheduled for 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC — reminder set for design/eng integration test.
